# A Fixture Paper on Citations

## Introduction

Paradigms shift when anomalies accumulate (Kuhn, 1962). Lending follows growth (Lindqvist and Berg, 2012). The same shift recurs (Kuhn, 1962).

Several studies agree (Lindqvist and Berg, 2012; Okafor, 2019). Trust can be measured (Okafor, 2019, p. 40). Networks persist (Okafor, 2019, p. 41).

## Discussion

Lindqvist and Berg (2012) argue that lending policy follows growth.

## Punctuation and Locators

Anomalies pile up (Kuhn, 1962)... Is lending growth-led (Lindqvist and Berg, 2012)?! Kuhn wrote of "the essential tension" (Kuhn, 1962). He asked "is it a paradigm?" (Kuhn, 1962). Lending stalls (in some years (Lindqvist and Berg, 2012)).

The pages are cited as a range (Okafor, 2019, pp. 33--38), an open run (Okafor, 2019, p. 33ff.). A chapter (Kuhn, 1962, chap. 2) and a section (Kuhn, 1962, sec. 3).

## Notes and Line Breaks

A prefixed note (see also Okafor, 2019). An abbreviation (e.g., Lindqvist and Berg, 2012). A suffix after a title (Okafor, 2019, emphasis added). A wrapped claim (Kuhn, 1962). A hard break (Lindqvist and Berg, 2012)\
on the next line. An ampersand run (Okafor, 2019)&more.

Emphasis in affixes (*see* Kuhn, 1962, p. 33, *emphasis added*), and a range (see Okafor, 2019, pp. 33--35 and *passim*).
